articles.title: Tesla is prepping a Cybercab onslaught | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The company is looking to roll the gold two-seater robotaxis out to other U.S. cities this year, even as it goes mum on the number of paid rides.
articles.body_text: Tesla says it is preparing to launch its shiny gold Cybercab in new markets outside its home of Austin, Texas, in a bid to “literally take over every part of terrestrial transportation.” “We’re starting with getting people from one place to the other, but we want to basically own transportation of any kind on Earth,” Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call Wednesday. Tesla has previously shown a concept version of a multi-passenger vehicle it calls the “Robovan,” but it’s unclear if Taneja’s bombastic comments mean the company is working on other types of transportation. What was clearer on the call is that Tesla’s Cybercab expansion will begin in Dallas next month and spread to other cities by the end of this year. Tesla already operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUV in small fleets in Dallas, Houston, and the Florida cities of Miami, Orlando, and Tampa. The company also said on its earnings call that it will start selling Cybercabs to fleet operators by the end of this year . Broader expansion of the Cybercab could set up a real fight with Waymo, which is currently the market leader for robotaxis in the United States, with more than 4,000 of them deployed across more than a dozen cities. Tesla has argued that its Cybercab is cheaper and easier to build, which should allow it to undercut Waymo and other robotaxi operators on price. But the company has to reach real scale outside Austin in order to prove that point. Tesla said it’s ready thanks to a dramatic increase in the number of miles its self-driving cars have traveled in recent weeks. While that may be true, Tesla was mum on Wednesday about how much money the overall robotaxi effort is bringing in. Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the new ride-hailing business won’t be noticeable in the company’s overall financial figures until the second quarter of 2027, “and probably a big deal by Q3 or Q4 of next year.” Tesla also made a change to its letter to shareholders that further obscures what little visibility there was into its robotaxi business. In Tesla’s second-quarter letter, the company included a chart for “Cumulative Paid Robotaxi Miles.” A close read of that chart showed a 36% decline from the first quarter of the year. In the new letter released on Wednesday, Tesla changed that chart to show “Cumulative Unsupervised Robotaxi Miles” — simpler indicator of how far the fleet cars are driving, whether or not they have paying riders on board. There wasn’t much more clarity on the call, either. When asked about paid robotaxi miles traveled, Taneja said the company is “seeing utilization improving,” but didn’t offer specifics. Instead, Taneja kept most of his comments generally focused on Tesla’s plans to scale the Cybercab. That included praise for Tesla’s engineering team for creating a vehicle that, according to the manufacturing team, is very easy to build — and build quickly. “They think this is one of the easiest products for them to scale in terms of manufacturing,” he said. “So scaling would not be that much of a challenge.” What might be a challenge, Taneja said, is that Tesla needs to make sure it has “all the regulatory approvals” so it can “start deploying the Cybercabs as fast as we can produce them.” That echoes many previous comments from Musk, who has long claimed that “regulatory approval” was the biggest barrier to Tesla’s robotaxi plans, not technical progress.

articles.title: Spotify confirms Family Plan crackdown, but calls it a 'routine improvement' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Spotify told investors its roll out of QR code verification to ensure Family Plan members live in the same household is not a "crackdown," just a routine improvement.
articles.body_text: Spotify confirmed the reports of its crackdown on Family Plan sharing during its third-quarter call with investors, calling its new method “a routine improvement” to its existing verification tools. Over the past several days, reports had surfaced indicating that Spotify was rolling out a “QR code verification” method, where the app would prompt members on its Family Plan to verify they lived with the plan manager by scanning a QR code. This code appears on the plan manager’s phone, which the plan member then needs to scan with their own phone, according to Spotify’s support documentation . Plan members have seven days to complete the QR code after getting a notification, which means they could be out of luck if they live outside the home and aren’t planning a return visit anytime soon. If the verification window is missed, they won’t be able to join another Family or Duo plan for 12 months, but would instead have to shift to an individual plan that they pay for themselves. The move is meant to boost subscriptions to Spotify’s profitable Premium plans, rather than allowing adult children or friends who live apart from gaming the system to get a cheaper plan by splitting a Family Plan subscription. During the earnings call, an investor asked a question about the crackdown and what it means, but Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström downplayed the change, calling it a “routine improvement,” not a “crackdown.” The executive said that the company’s attempt to better verify its users is not something that would have an end date or would ever be complete, but would be considered an ongoing routine improvement. articles.title: Investors break down how founders can raise a Series A today | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Raising a Series A these days isn't so simple — top investors break down what founders need to know now.
articles.body_text: In today’s market, no single metric defines what a Series A is, or how to raise one. At this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt, three investors offered founders advice on raising one, and one of them tacked on a warning. With money pouring into AI and revenue numbers being inflated to justify sky-high valuations, a correction could come as soon as 2027. The warning came from Shailendra Singh, a managing director at Peak XV, who spoke alongside Jahanvi Sardana, a partner at Index Ventures, and Jenelle Teng Wade, a partner at Bessemer. “Seed and venture, I’ve never seen it as dysfunctional as it is now,” Singh said, adding that the current market is one of the hardest to raise in that he has seen. “The burden is high to convince any top firm that you are amongst the few special companies that can break out, and then the dispersion is very high on the terms you might get, how much capital you can raise, and what terms you can raise it,” he continued. In fact, it’s common now to see a company trying to close a round with as many as three different prices at once. “[I]’s a crazy sign of market froth,” he said. “We’re calling it the ‘tranchopalooza,’” Sardana added, referring to the way rounds are being split into tranches, or separate chunks. Beyond the warnings, the investors laid out what they look for in a Series A pitch, including, first, a persuasive story about why a founder has a shot at building a big company. “Founders who can attract very high-quality talent have an advantage,” Singh added. What a founder builds matters, too. Teng Wade said capital is flowing into areas such as defense, robotics, and AI infrastructure. She also noted that foundational model companies are moving toward vertical integration (taking on more of the stack themselves), but there’s still room for newer players, including neo-clouds that rent out AI computing power and neo-labs focused on AI research. Metrics, meanwhile, still help a lot, but they are less defined than they used to be, especially in an era like AI where it’s incredibly expensive to run a company. Teng Wade gave an example of how her firm evaluated Anthropic in its early days, when its margins were negative, and it was spending heavily on compute. One partner on her team, however, felt that AI was going to be “bigger than everything we’ve ever expected in terms of price premium on the frontier models,” she said, “becoming a substitute for other types of software.” The logic was that even with money-losing margins, the market would be big enough to pay off if the company became one of the top three players. Anthropic is now reportedly preparing an IPO at a valuation of around $2 trillion . It told investors this month it was profitable on an adjusted basis , though that measure excludes some costs. The investors also spoke about the importance of honesty in a market like this, where inflated annual recurring revenue (ARR) numbers are swirling alongside headline valuations. “I tell founders, If you ever show a chart which shows cumulative revenue or cumulative ARR, that is a massive red flag,” Singh said. “It means that your time series data is not good because cumulative data is a big lie.” Added Singh: It’s important for a company to be intellectually honest in how they are presenting and engaging in bull cycles.” Singh said the market is full of “false positives” because “it can’t be that every company is going to be successful. This is as optimistic as I’ve seen the venture world in two decades, and normally it’s a sign. I think 2027 will be different. I think we will see a correction.” Finally, the panelists were asked to give founders at least one piece of parting advice. Singh went first, reminding founders that building a company is one of the “most excruciatingly difficult things” one can do. And with that, “deal with it,” he said. He also urged founders not to rush into something, to watch out for weak product-market fit, and always hold the bar very high for what they are trying to solve. Sardana said it is important to know how to pitch but that founders should be careful not to let that dictate what they build. “It feels like [founders are] deciding what to build based on what’s getting funded, which is really scary,” she continued. Teng Wade, meanwhile, said her typical advice of telling founders to be conservative with their projections and requests hasn’t really held up.

articles.title: Fusion startup Helion is developing new semiconductors that could double output of its power plants | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Helion now has another $225 million to help speed development of its first fusion power plant, due to provide Microsoft with electricity in 2028.
articles.body_text: Fusion startup Helion has been awarded $175 million in federal funding to research, develop, and manufacture advanced semiconductors and power electronics for its fusion power plants, the company announced on Thursday. Currently, those devices lose about 5% to 10% of the electricity that flows through them. While those losses seem small, they can compound themselves in a complex system like Helion’s. “If we can cut that loss in half, that’s actually twice the power output of the fusion system,” David Kirtley, co-founder and CEO at Helion, told TechCrunch. Helion has been racing to complete its first power plant, Orion, in time to meet a 2028 deadline to provide Microsoft with electricity from the grid. Funding from the award will help Helion build automated semiconductor module, packaging, and testing capacity to supply the fusion machine that’s currently under construction. The new production line, to be built in Washington State, will be the first in the U.S. to make a class of semiconductor that is used not just in fusion power, but in manufacturing, wastewater treatment, medicine, and defense. “There are no U.S. manufacturers right now that do it,” Kirtley said. “This is absolutely enabling going from zero to 100 for advanced, high-voltage, and pulsed semiconductors here in the United States.” The three-year award was made by the Department of Commerce under the CHIPS Act, a Biden-era law that seeks to bolster semiconductor module research, development, and manufacturing in the U.S. Alongside the federal funding, Helion also announced a fresh $50 million private investment, though it didn’t disclose the investor. In total, Helion has raised more than $3.2 billion, making it the second-best-funded fusion startup . More than $100 million will be set aside for semiconductor and advanced packaging R&D in Washington State, while approximately $80 million will support R&D efforts in Vermont for advanced semiconductor tooling, design, and process development with GlobalFoundries, Kirtley told TechCrunch. Separately, GlobalFoundries has received more than $80 million from the federal government to advance the manufacturing of gallium-nitride semiconductors, a type that is widely used in power electronics. Kirtley acknowledged that the R&D funded by the award won’t make its way into Orion in time for the launch — federal contracts can take months to negotiate — but he said they promise to help improve the efficiency of subsequent Helion power plants, which would improve their competitiveness in cutthroat electricity markets. Semiconductor efficiency is key to Helion’s approach to fusion, which harvests electricity directly from the fusion reactions rather than using them to heat steam to spin a turbine. The startup is developing a reactor known as a field-reversed configuration. Fusion fuel gets injected into both ends of an hourglass-like chamber, where it’s heated to form a plasma. The plasmas are then accelerated toward each other using magnetic fields. When they collide, another magnetic field compresses the ball further, raising the temperature to over 100 million degrees C. At those temperatures and pressures, atoms in the fusion fuel start fusing, releasing energy in the process, and pushing the plasma outward. This force pushes against the magnetic field, and that energy is captured by the magnets and capacitors and turned into electricity — think of how a hybrid car or EV recharges the battery by using electric motors to slow the vehicle.

articles.title: Meta wants to pay for its broad AI buildout with a newly created class of stock | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The social media giant is planning a new stock strategy to help power its broad investments in AI models and services.
articles.body_text: Meta is making a big push into AI, and it’s creating a new kind of stock that could help pay for it. On Wednesday, as the company reported its third-quarter earnings, Semafor reported the company might issue non-voting stock, meaning shares that don’t give their owners a vote on company decisions, to help fund its push into artificial intelligence. During Meta’s earnings call, the company confirmed that reporting. Meta’s chief financial officer, Susan Li, said the company plans to “create a new class of non-voting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders through a stock dividend.” Li later added that the company “created this new class of shares with the purpose of creating a publicly traded non-voting stock usable for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes while preserving the voting power of existing Class A and B shareholders.” The shares will allow the company to maintain its current “founder-led structure,” she added. They will also expand its “funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business, driven by AI.” Meta’s earnings were strong this past quarter, beating Wall Street expectations. The company made $64 billion in revenue, a jump of 26% from a year earlier. Its costs and expenses also rose, however, by 68% year-over-year. Reality Labs, the division responsible for Meta’s AR glasses, VR headsets, and VR software, continues to lose money, though less than it used to. The company said in its earnings report that it expects the division’s losses to shrink from its 2025 levels to between $18 billion and $19 billion. Meta has made a big push into AI over the past year. The company has released several AI models, including Muse Spark and Muse Glimmer earlier this year. In recent weeks, it added Muse Wonder and Muse Spark Open, an open-weight model whose underlying parameters are publicly available for outsiders to use and build on. Meta also launched a coding agent for software developers called Muse Code. At its Meta Connect event this year, the company announced a new line of cute and cuddly avatars for AI assistant, Meta Muse, in a push to make its AI services more relatable (and also meme-able ). As far as can be discerned, those AI products are doing well. “In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada have set up Muse personal agents,” CEO Mark Zuckerberg said during Wednesday’s earnings call. “Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number one in the App Store almost every day.” “Now that Muse has clear product-market fit, we are entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling it,” Zuckerberg added, claiming later that the company expects to grow the product’s appeal to eventually “serve billions of people.” The company also noted that certain storm clouds linger on the horizon in the form of ongoing regulatory and legal issues. “We continue to monitor active legal and regulatory matters that could significantly impact our business and financial results,” said Li. “For example, we continue to see scrutiny on youth-related issues in several markets, and have a number of youth-related trials scheduled in the coming months in the United States.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Airbnb limits chores for guests, sparking backlash from hosts | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Hosts are threatening to leave the platform after Airbnb says that they can no longer require guests to strip beds or do other time-consuming cleaning chores.
articles.body_text: Airbnb is taking steps to limit the chores that hosts can require of guests prior to checkout, addressing a long-standing grievance among customers who often pay cleaning fees and are told they must do a list of tasks themselves. In a new policy update , Airbnb prohibits hosts from mandating that guests strip beds, wash and put away dishes, start laundry, or remove trash from the property. This new guideline will apply to reservations made on or after November 20. This change comes in response to years of backlash regarding overly burdensome checkout instructions and hefty fines for not disposing of trash. Many guests have voiced their frustrations on social media, questioning why they should be responsible for cleaning tasks after already paying a cleaning fee. However, some hosts aren’t pleased with the update. Within Airbnb’s community forums , some argue that basic cleaning responsibilities are essential for maintaining sanitary conditions and protecting their properties. They point out that hosts must manage the costs and practical demands of preparing their properties for the next guests. One host expressed concern that the new policy leans toward a hotel-like model, which detracts from the unique appeal of Airbnb. “Guests are given complete freedom to be lazy while the hosts bear the risk,” the host wrote. “The major distinction between commercial hotels and my private home is the personal touch. Guests can certainly be expected to wash their dishes or put them in the dishwasher and remove their dirty linens. In exchange, they enjoy a personal connection and a unique environment that a hotel simply can’t provide. Plus, every potential guest has the opportunity to read the listing beforehand and decide what they prefer. If these restrictions are removed, it could lead me to withdraw my listing and bid farewell to Airbnb after twelve years.” Airbnb has outlined some exceptions to the new policy, though. Hosts may still ask guests to conserve water during droughts or use bear-proof trash containers in areas where wildlife poses a risk. The policy change highlights the challenge Airbnb faces in balancing the expectations of guests versus hosts and is another step taken in addressing guests’ concerns. The company faced scrutiny in 2024 over price transparency from hosts tacking on cleaning fees after guests booked their listings. In 2023, the company said more than 260,000 hosts had reduced or eliminated their cleaning fees. In May 2025, Airbnb began displaying total prices — including fees but excluding taxes — by default in search results worldwide. It will be interesting to see how many hosts decide the new restrictions make Airbnb less attractive as a platform. But the move could also draw in more travelers who want the convenience of a rental without feeling as though they are both paying for housecleaning while still expected to clean the home themselves. articles.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself.
articles.body_text: Recursive , an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint , on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI. Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months. Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop. The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist. Because Flint runs on a user’s own computer rather than a company’s cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the usage fees that AI cloud services charge based on how much text the model processes. The model is free to download on Hugging Face, the popular site for sharing AI models, under the Apache 2.0 license, an open source license that allows free use and modification. Flint is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning it uses only a small slice of itself for any given task: just 2.5 billion of its 40 billion settings, known as parameters, at a time. That makes it light enough for an ordinary laptop and far smaller than Meta’s Muse Spark Open , an open model built for Macs that was released last week. Muse Spark Open uses 816 billion parameters and needs at least a terabyte of memory. Flint is also fast. In Recursive’s tests, it generated about 131 tokens (chunks of text) per second on a MacBook Pro with Apple’s M4 Pro chip — roughly twice the 58 to 69 tokens per second that similar models managed on the same machine, including Google’s Gemma 4 and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. On Nvidia’s RTX Spark, Flint topped 150 tokens per second. On SWE-Bench Verified, a benchmark that measures how well AI can fix real-world software bugs, Flint outperformed other models under 50 billion parameters. On Recursive’s own average across six tests, only one model, Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 27B, scored higher than Flint. The company acknowledged that Flint would need more guidance than the big paid coding assistants and suggested breaking large tasks into smaller steps. Still, early reviews were positive. Wired’s Will Knight used Flint on a Mac with 48GB of memory to build several small programs, including a to-do list app and a tool that scours the web for research. He found that smaller coding models often ran into errors or were slow compared to Claude or Codex, but Flint nailed his coding requests every time. The Eureka Machine comes up with ideas, runs experiments, and uses the results to decide what to try next. According to the company’s launch video , it contributed to nearly every part of building Flint, from pretraining to post-training and inference. Recursive said that Eureka’s contributions include a sparser model shape, low-bit training that shrank Flint by 71% with almost no loss in quality and custom kernels, which are specialized programs that speed up the underlying computations. Recursive didn’t say how much time the Eureka Machine saved its researchers, but it’s not alone in leaning on AI to do research. OpenAI said last month that by mid-August, its AI agents were logging 3.1 workdays for every one worked by a human researcher.

articles.title: FRA: Kan inte utesluta intrång i Sverige
articles.summary: En säkerhetslucka skakar om internet och det larmas om miljontals angreppsförsök globalt sett. Enligt FRA går det inte att utesluta att intrång skett i Sverige. – Det skulle nästan vara osannolikt om inte detta har utnyttjats på något sätt, säger Ola Billger, kommunikationschef.
articles.body_text: En säkerhetslucka skakar om internet och det larmas om miljontals angreppsförsök globalt sett. Enligt FRA går det inte att utesluta att intrång skett i Sverige. – Det skulle nästan vara osannolikt om inte detta har utnyttjats på något sätt, säger Ola Billger, kommunikationschef hos myndigheten. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Experter v arnar för en våg av hackerattacker och det har redan rapporterats om miljontals angreppsförsök. Försvarets radioanstalt ( FRA ), som är en del av Sveriges underrättelse- och säkerhetstjänst, uppger att man följer utvecklingen noga. – Det här är en sårbarhet som är väldigt spridd i och med att så många webbplatser använder php, säger Ola Billger, kommunikationschef på myndigheten. På onsdagseftermiddagen släpptes en uppdatering och flera länder, däribland Finland, Danmark och Nederländerna stängde ner sina myndighetssajter i väntan på den. Totalt använder 330 000 aktiva hemsidor php i Sverige, enligt analysverktyget Builtwith . Här har Nationellt cybersäkerhetscenter, en del av FRA, uppmanat verksamheter att uppdatera sina system omgående eller koppla bort dem från internet. – Min bild av de samtal vi har haft med olika verksamhetsutövare är att man uppdaterar och följer rekommendationerna, säger Ola Billger. Det är oklart hur många svenska myndigheter, om några, som stängde ner sina sajter.

articles.title: Åklagarens kritik: Lagstiftningen har inte hängt med
articles.summary: Den svenska lagstiftningen är inte anpassad efter hur dagens arbetsplatser ser ut. Det menar åklagaren Christer B Jarlås. – Det är konstigt att det här inte är prioriterat. Ingen tycker väl att man ska dö på jobbet, säger han.
articles.body_text: Den svenska lagstiftningen är inte anpassad efter hur dagens arbetsplatser ser ut. – Det är konstigt att det här inte är prioriterat. Ingen tycker väl att man ska dö på jobbet, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Hittills i år har 26 personer, 4 kvinnor och 22 män, gått till jobbet i Sverige – men sen inte kommit hem igen. Christer B Jarlås är åklagare på Riksenheten för miljö- och arbetsmiljömål (REMA), och har 30 års erfarenhet av att jobba med den här typen av ”otäcka händelser”. Och han tycker inte att lagstiftningen har hängt med. – Vår lagstiftning utgår från hur en arbetsplats såg ut för kanske 40–50 år sen. Den utgår från att det är ett företag som är ansvarigt för en arbetsplats och tar inte hänsyn till de långa entreprenörskedjor som finns i dag, säger Jarlås. Detta är en kritik som ofta lyfts, även från fackligt håll. Och det handlar framför allt om byggarbetsplatser – som är extra utsatta när det kommer till dödsolyckor i arbetet – där det i dag kan finnas dussintals underentreprenörer på en och samma arbetsplats. Enligt kritikerna riskerar det försämra arbetsmiljöarbetet, om en helentreprenör anlitar billiga underentreprenörer och inte ställer tillräckliga krav på dem. – De som ytterst tjänar pengar kommer ganska lätt undan ansvar, säger Christer B Jarlås. På en arbetsplats är det de enskilda företagen som ansvarar för sina anställdas arbetsmiljö, men det skulle REMA-åklagaren vilja ändra på. Han drar en parallell till medievärlden, där en ansvarig utgivare är juridiskt ansvarig för allt innehåll som publiceras.

articles.title: M-toppen: Det blir ingen fyradagarsvecka
articles.summary: Stjärnskottet Oliver Rosengren blir Moderaternas talesperson i arbetsmarknadsfrågor. Han vill att svenskarna ska jobba hårdare – och räds inte ett extraval.
articles.body_text: Stjärnskottet Oliver Rosengren blir Moderaternas talesperson i arbetsmarknadsfrågor. Han vill att svenskarna ska jobba hårdare – och räds inte ett extraval. – Det blir inga fyradagarsveckor i mitt Sverige, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Moderaternas riksdagsledamot Oliver Rosengren, 34, blev kommunalråd i Växjö redan som 24-åring och utsågs fyra år senare av Expressen till Sveriges mäktigaste politiker under 30 år . Nu gör han sin andra mandatperiod i riksdagen, och tar över ansvaret för arbetsmarknadsfrågorna inom Moderaterna som ny gruppledare i arbetsmarknadsutskottet. Efter Tidöregeringens fokus på brott och invandring är det nu dags att flytta fram partiets positioner i frågan om fler jobb och en växande ekonomi, tycker Rosengren. Han har tidigare ingått i en arbetsgrupp som tagit fram en rad större reformer på arbetsmarknadsområdet, bland annat att försörjningsstödet ska ersättas av ett arbetslöshetsbidrag, som likt a-kassan ska ha tydliga avtrappningar. Oliver Rosengren anser att de rödgröna partierna lurar svenska folket att tro att det går att jobba mindre. – Det går inte att få det bättre utan att anstränga sig mer. Ska vi klara Sveriges utmaningar framåt är det beska svaret at vi behöver arbeta mer, säger han. Trots många år i toppolitiken har Oliver Rosengren även några andra erfarenheter på sitt cv. – Mitt första jobb som många andra unga var på Max hamburgare, man lär sig hantera stress och press, och vara trevlig även om andra inte är trevliga tillbaka. Jag har också varit vikarie på en förskola, säger han, och tillägger: – Men jag har inte sprungit i trappor som hemtjänstpersonal eller stått vid industribandet. Därför försöker jag lägga mycket tid på att vara ute. Under förra mandatperioden gjorde jag över 500 företagsbesök, framför allt i Kronobergs län, för att skaffa mig inblick i vilka behov som finns.

articles.title: Sigtunaskolans vd: Finns ingen våldskultur
articles.summary: Flera elever på Sigtunaskolan misstänks ha utsatt andra elever för våldsbrott. Skolans vd säger till SvD att det ”absolut inte” finns någon våldskultur i skolan.
articles.body_text: Flera elever på Sigtunaskolan misstänks ha utsatt andra elever för våldsbrott. Skolans vd säger till SvD att det ”absolut inte” finns någon våldskultur i skolan. – Jag tror på internatskolor, säger Sofia Kinberg. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Incidenten som ägde rum på Sigtunaskolan tidigare i oktober har skakat om internatet. Fem elever är misstänkta för att ha utsatt flera andra elever för kränkningar och sexuellt våld. I samband med att det uppmärksammats har flera andra vittnesmål inifrån skolan kommit fram. Expressen har tidigare skrivit om Michael som berättade att äldre elever tvingade honom krypa runt halvnaken i hundkoppel och äta spyor ur en hink under sin tid på skolan. Expressen har flera gånger sökt skolans ledning som inte velat svara på frågor. Men till SvD talar nu Sigtunaskolans vd, Sofia Kingberg, ut. Hon säger att de senaste veckorna varit omtumlande och att skolans ledning är chockerade över allt som hänt. – Vi har svårt att förstå hur det har kunnat hända, säger hon. Kinberg säger att ledningen vetat om att det historiskt funnits kränkningar på skolan och att de arbetat aktivt för att få bort ”all form av informella maktstrukturer och kränkningar”. Hon anser dock att det är för tidigt att svara på om de senaste brotten är en del av en maktstruktur. Åklagare Lisa dos Santos är förundersökningsledare i brottsutredningen. Hon säger att de misstänkta gärningarna är begångna på skolan och att det verkar vara del av en struktur. – Det är någonting som verkar höra hemma under det här så kallade maktsystemet, att äldre elever tar sig rätten att kontrollera och tvinga yngre elever att göra som de säger helt enkelt, och i något fall kanske eventuellt med bestraffningar, säger hon. Att det skulle finnas en kultur av våld på skolan anser inte vd:n Kinberg.

När han på torsdagen var på plats i riksdagen för sin första arbetsdag gjorde han en rad intervjuer med SVT, TV4, ETC och Aftonbladet. När Expressen till sist fick möjlighet att ställa frågor valde Vänsterpartiets pressekreterare Maria Carlsson att avbryta intervjun efter bara några frågor. Vi har under flera veckor skickat frågor till dig. Varför har du inte svarat på dem? – Det har varit under lite extra påfrestning som jag haft de senaste fyra veckorna. Jag kunde inte svara på varje meddelande eller varje mejl. Jag har inte svarat alls, säger Mohamed Ali. Vi har ställt viktiga frågor om dina skulder. Är det inte bra att ge läsarna din bild av det här? Varför har du blivit så skuldsatt? – Jag har meddelat det till Expressen förut. Jag har ansökt om omprövning digitalt för att betala mina skulder så fort jag kan. Men hans ansökan om omprövning kom in först efter att Expressen avslöjat att kreditbolaget Sergel redan ansökt om omprövning av skuldsaneringen, och krävt att han omedelbart skulle betala. – Ja, men de senaste fyra veckorna, som sagt, har varit mycket påfrestande. Jag mådde dåligt, jag kunde inte ringa till myndigheterna och sånt. Men när jag har haft den där tiden, har jag ringt dem och ansökt om omprövningen. För att jag gör rätt för mig.

articles.title: Generaldirektören pressas om fallet
articles.summary: Efter Expressens avslöjanden om sexuella kränkningar och otrygghet på kvinnofängelset i Ystad kallades Kriminalvårdens högste chef till riksdagen.
articles.body_text: Efter Expressens avslöjanden om sexuella kränkningar och otrygghet på kvinnofängelset i Ystad kallades Kriminalvårdens högste chef till riksdagen. Där pressades generaldirektör Rikard Jermsten om varför det dröjde innan livstidsdömda Lily Abdelshahed flyttades till en mansanstalt. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Efter drygt en timme bakom stängda dörrar kommer Kriminalvårdens generaldirektör Rikard Jermsten ut från riksdagens justitieutskott. Där har han fått svara på frågor om allt från svenska fångar i Estland och utbyggnaden av anstalter till det uppmärksammade fallet med barnamördaren Lily Abdelshahed, 39. Efter Expressens granskning av sexuella kränkningar och otrygghet på kvinnofängelset i Ystad har den livstidsdömda barnmördaren nu flyttats tillbaka till en mansanstalt. Men varför dröjde det så länge innan Kriminalvården agerade? – Jag har full förståelse för att man kan tycka att det kan ta för lång tid. Men vår interna bedömning av situationen har inte varit exakt den som man ger uttryck för i massmedia, säger Rikard Jermsten. Expressen har i flera artiklar granskat situationen på kvinnoanstalten Ystad, dit Lily Abdelshahed flyttades förra hösten efter att ha bytt juridiskt kön. Kvinnliga intagna har berättat för Expressen om sexuella kränkningar och en rädsla som påverkat deras vardag. Flera har undvikit gemensamma utrymmen, bland annat duscharna som inte går att låsa. – Lily är lång, bred och skäggig och går runt i för kort nattsärk och visar snoppen, som dinglar fritt, berättade en fånge. Även kriminalvårdare och facket har slagit larm.

Expressen avslöjade i lördags att en personlig assistent misstänks ha misshandlat en 50-årig funktionsnedsatt man i Alingsås . Våldet fångades på film. Men kommunen dröjde tre veckor med att polisanmäla händelsen. Först efter att Expressen inlett sin granskning gjordes en anmälan. Socialtjänstminister Camilla Waltersson Grönvall (M) reagerar på uppgifterna. ” Det får aldrig råda något tvivel om att samhällets mest sårbara individer ska vara trygga och mötas av respekt och omsorg. Kommunernas ansvar är inte förhandlingsbart. Allt våld måste tas på största allvar och mötas av kraftfulla åtgärder. Att en misstänkt misshandel inte polisanmäldes direkt, trots att det fanns en film på händelsen, är djupt oroande.” Expressen kan nu avslöja ytterligare ett fall av missförhållanden inom assistansvården i Alingsås. Den 8 december 2025 slog personal larm till en LSS-chef i Alingsås om allvarliga brister i omsorgen om en funktionsnedsatt kvinna. Larmet gällde en personlig assistent i 30-årsåldern som misstänktes ha misskött sitt arbete. Enligt kommunens utredning ska kvinnan, som är i 40-årsåldern, vid upprepade tillfällen ha lämnats liggande nerkissad i sängen under längre perioder. Det fanns också uppgifter om uteblivna duschar och bristande rengöring efter inkontinens och avföring. Men bristerna handlade inte bara om hygienen.

articles.title: Svensk-kurdisk politiker släppt
articles.summary: Den svensk-kurdiska politikern Lütfi Baksi, 83, greps turkisk polis på flygplatsen i Istanbul. Nu har han släppts. Det uppger hans son Kurdo Baksi.
articles.body_text: Den svensk-kurdiska politikern Lütfi Baksi, 83, greps turkisk polis på flygplatsen i Istanbul. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Den svensk-kurdiska politikern Lütfi Baksi, 83, greps på onsdagen vid lunchtid. Han kunde sedan släppas på torsdagen, meddelar hans son Kurdo Baksi. – Jag är så glad att min far kunde lämna häktet. Jag hoppas han kan flyga till Stockholm utan några problem. Vad jag vet har han inget utreseförbud från Turkiet men man vet aldrig. Jag och familjen kan bli lugna först när han landar på Arlanda, säger han i en kommentar. Lütfi Baksi är bland annat före detta partiledare för partiet Kadep. Han har tidigare dömts till 6,5 års fängelse. Domen har överklagats. Kurdo Baksi kommenterade tidigare faderns gripande: – Jag är förvånad över att min far frihetsberövats. Turkiet sitter i fredsförhandlingar med PKK men jagar en 83-årig svårt sjuk människorättskämpe. Min far straffas bara för att han har använt sig av sin yttrandefrihet. Han har bara haft åsikter. Han har alltid föredragit att kämpa med fredliga medel och tagit avstånd från våld. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. Expressen granskar, avslöjar och ger dig senaste nyheterna på ett sakligt sätt.
